```

If `replicate` cannot use relay against the target, it fails and tells you to rerun with `sync`.

For very large initial migrations, add `--target-max-pack-bytes` to split the initial pack into multiple smaller batches. The same flag works on `sync`, since `sync` auto-bootstraps on empty targets:

```bash
git-sync sync \
  --target-max-pack-bytes 536870912 \
  --protocol v2 \
  -v \
  <source-url> \
  <target-url>
```

A bootstrap from a `github.com` source that is not given `--target-max-pack-bytes` first asks the GitHub REST API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}`) for the repository size. It sends the source credentials git-sync holds at that point, so a private repository answers too: a `--source-token`, a `user:token@` in the source URL, or credentials the git credential helper supplied when the git server asked for them. A public repository never asks, so with only a credential helper its lookup stays anonymous and counts against GitHub's anonymous rate limit. When GitHub reports 1.5 GiB or more, the bootstrap switches to batches of 512 MiB (or `--max-pack-bytes`, if smaller); a reported size of 0 (an empty repository, or one GitHub has not sized yet) keeps a single pack. A token the API refuses (401 or 403) is retried once without credentials, which is enough for a public repository. When the lookup fails anyway — no credentials for a private repository, an exhausted rate limit, an unreachable API — the bootstrap starts with a single pack and git-sync prints a notice naming the cause, including the refusal when a token was refused first. The bootstrap can still switch to batches later if the target rejects the pack as too large. The outcome, including the HTTP status or error, goes to the library's `Options.BootstrapLogger`, at warning level when the lookup failed, and a successful lookup is also logged with `-v`. Pass `--target-max-pack-bytes` to choose batching yourself and skip the lookup.
38:- **A private GitHub repository over 1.5 GiB now bootstraps in batches.** The GitHub repository-size lookup that selects batched bootstrap sent no credentials, so GitHub answered 404 for every private repository and the bootstrap silently sent the whole repository as one pack, whatever its size. The lookup now carries the source credentials it holds for the API host — an explicit token, a `user:token@` in the source URL, or credentials the git credential helper supplied when the git server asked for them — which also moves token-authenticated public lookups off the anonymous rate limit shared by everything behind the same IP. A token the API refuses (401/403) is retried once anonymously, so a public repository is never worse off, and the refusal is reported if the retry fails too. Credentials are never sent with TLS verification off, nor when they were looked up for a host a redirect led to. Each lookup's outcome (HTTP status or error, reported size, chosen mode) is now logged through `Options.BootstrapLogger` without verbose mode, at warning level when the size could not be determined, and a failed lookup prints a notice that the bootstrap starts with a single pack. A `github.com` URL on a non-default port is no longer treated as GitHub, so its credentials never reach the GitHub API. ([#124](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/124))

416:### Indivisible bootstrap upload fallback
They are sent to that host, and to subdomains of it on the same port, and
nowhere else. A redirect from `http` to `https` on the same host keeps them —
that is an upgrade — but a redirect from `https` to `http` does not.

This matters with `--source-follow-info-refs-redirect` /
`--target-follow-info-refs-redirect`, which send follow-up RPCs to the host that
`/info/refs` redirected to. A redirect within the same site (say `example.com`
to `replica.example.com`, the hosting-replica case the flag exists for) keeps
your credentials. A redirect to an unrelated host does not: git-sync withholds
them, prints a warning naming the host, and consults the git credential helper
for that host instead. So a redirect you did not intend — an open redirect on the
real host, a hostile mirror, or a man-in-the-middle on a plain-`http` source —
cannot collect your token.

If a redirect target legitimately needs credentials and is not same-site, store
them in your git credential helper against that host; git-sync will find them

The review found 14 items. None blocks merging, but three are worth fixing, and one of those is a problem my nit-fix commit made worse. It ran at xhigh because it didn't read "high" from my arguments. It confirmed findings 1 and 3 by running a throwaway test.

**Worth fixing**

| # | Finding | My take |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | An auth method that puts credentials in a header other than `Authorization` leaks them on a redirect to another site. The redirect guard only removes `Authorization`. | Real. The guard has always behaved this way for git requests too, but my `applyAuth`/`carriesAny` change and the `headerAuth` test now present custom headers as supported. **Revert that change** and go back to checking only `Authorization`; that is finding 12's suggestion too. Fixing the guard itself is a separate PR. |
| 2 | GitHub reporting size 0 is logged at INFO as "empty repository". But bootstrap only runs when the source has refs, so 0 really means GitHub hasn't sized the repo yet. | Real. It is the same silent single pack this PR exists to surface, for a freshly pushed large repo. Treat 0 as an unknown size, so it warns and prints the notice. |
| 3 | Pressing Ctrl-C during the lookup prints the "could not read the GitHub repository size … single pack" notice. | Real and confirmed, though minor. Skip the notice and warning when the run's own context is cancelled. |

**Cheap hardening, I'd take these too**

- **4:** transport and TLS error text goes into the notice without cleaning. A certificate's hostnames can carry an escape character. Run the whole reason through `cleanServerMessage`.
- **5:** a 401/403 counts as "credentials refused" even when the answering request carried no credentials, for example after a redirect stripped them. Only treat it as a refusal when the request was authenticated.
- **6:** the 30s timeout covers both attempts, so a slow 403 leaves the anonymous retry about 2s. Give each attempt its own timeout.

**Low value or design choices**

- **7:** a transport error is logged `authenticated=true`. I think that's defensible, since the credentials were sent.
- **8:** `CredentialsFor` would panic if the endpoint URL were nil. No current caller can hit this, but a nil check costs one line.
- **9:** a token written as a bare username (`https://ghp_xxx@github.com/...`) is never sent to the API. The PR skips bare usernames on purpose, but this URL form is common, and those private repos will now print a notice on every bootstrap. **Your call:** keep skipping them, or send usernames that start with a GitHub token prefix (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghs_`, `github_pat_`).
- **10:** library callers with no progress reporter get the notice on stderr in addition to the warning in their `BootstrapLogger`. Worth considering for servers that mirror many repos.
- **11–14:** refactors:
  - extend the existing `sanitize` package instead of adding a second cleaner;
  - move the GitHub API client out of `bootstrap.go`;
  - flatten the repeated failure checks in `logGitHubPreflight`.
  
  The first two are reasonable follow-ups, not for this PR.

Shall I apply 1–6 (and 8) and push? For 9, do you want to keep skipping bare-username tokens, or send them when they have a GitHub token prefix?

I fixed findings 1–6 and 8 and pushed them to PR #124 as commit `8f7b1d1f`. The full test suite, the race tests on the two affected packages, and golangci-lint all pass. I also updated the PR description to match.

- **1, custom auth headers:** I reverted my earlier change and the `headerAuth` test, so `authenticated` checks only `Authorization` again. That matches what the redirect guard strips.
- **2, size 0:** a reported size of 0 now counts as unknown, so it logs a warning and prints the notice.

- **4, unclean error text:** every error that reaches the log or the notice is now cleaned, transport errors included.
- **5, false refusal:** a 401/403 counts as a refused token only when the request that got it still carried the credentials. If a redirect stripped them, there is no retry and no blame on the token.
- **6, shared timeout:** each attempt now gets its own 30s timeout. To test this I turned the timeout constant into a variable.
- **8, nil endpoint:** `CredentialsFor` now returns nil instead of panicking when the connection has no endpoint URL.

Each fix has a new test. I wrote them all before the code, but I only saw the nil-endpoint test fail on its own. The rest went in together and couldn't compile until the timeout became a variable, so I never watched them fail against the old code.

Then assert that the second attempt's deadline is later than the first's and lands about `githubPreflightTimeout` after it started. This needs no sleeps.      - **Cost:** one parse per bootstrap, nanoseconds. Leave it.
  
  5. **`bootstrap.go:582-636` (`logGitHubPreflight`)** builds the attrs slice and runs `cleanServerMessage` even when both loggers are nil.

     def := map[string]string{"https": "443", "http": "80"}[ep.Scheme]

     ```

  **internal/gitproto/smarthttp.go**

     - **Cost today:** about 3 lines per test, around 40 lines in total.

     - **Redirect tests:** `RedirectDropsCredentials` (L652) and `UnauthenticatedRefusalIsNotRetried` (L564) both build an "elsewhere" TLS server with a hit counter and a `repoAPI` that redirects to it. Only elsewhere's response differs. A helper `redirectingAPI(t, respond) (*http.Client, *int)` removes about 10 lines from each.

I applied the cleanups and committed them locally as `80471802`; it isn't pushed yet. All tests pass, including the race detector on the three changed packages, and golangci-lint reports 0 issues. Behaviour is unchanged: same log fields, notice text and credential rules.

**Fixed:**
- **Own file:** the GitHub preflight code now lives in `internal/strategy/bootstrap/github_preflight.go`. That takes about 300 lines out of `bootstrap.go`.
- **One sanitizer:** the message cleaner is now `sanitize.Line` in the shared `sanitize` package, with a test. The package doc now explains how it differs from `sanitize.Text`. Bootstrap no longer has its own copy.
- **`authOrigin`:** explicit credentials now get it set when the connection is created, so `CredentialsFor` reads one field instead of branching. The same three lines for adopting helper credentials were in two places; they now share one helper, `adoptHelperCreds`.
- **Default port:** `GitHubOwnerRepo` now uses the existing default-port rule through a new `gitproto.UsesDefaultPort`, instead of a second copy.
- **Smaller simplifications:**
  - `logGitHubPreflight` checks for failure once instead of three times.
  - `githubAPIError` has one fallback path instead of two.
  - A nil check that could never trigger is gone.
  - The `lookupGitHubRepoSize` doc is shorter, and the shared `samesite.go` doc no longer names GitHub.
- **Tests:**
  - The timeout test no longer sleeps: it checks that the retry gets its own, later deadline. The bootstrap package tests went from 1.7s to 0.3s, and the timeout is a constant again.
  - The size-0 case is now a row in the unusable-body table.
  - New `captureNotices` and `redirectingAPI` helpers replace repeated setup.
  - The bearer-token test reuses `privateRepoAPI`.
  - An older test now uses `useGitHubAPI`.

**Skipped:**
- **A separate `internal/github` package and a gitproto helper that sends requests to sibling services:** both would reach callers outside this PR. Moving the code to its own file covers most of the benefit.
- **Applying `sanitize.Line`'s stricter rules to `sanitize.Text`:** that would change about 8 other callers. Worth its own PR if you think the encoded-C1 risk is real.
- **Cleaning the GitHub message only once:** `githubAPIError` needs the cleaned length to truncate it, and cleaning twice is harmless.
- **Draining the response body, and making the tests parallel:** negligible gain. Running in parallel would also mean moving package globals into `Params`.

Shall I push it to the PR?

Concise output style is active. Be concise: lead with the result, skip preamble and narration, keep only what the user needs.

I fixed the panic and pushed it to PR #124 as `19751f45`. My simplify pass caused it: I removed the nil check on `resp.Request` because one of the review agents said Go always sets it. It doesn't — Go's own client code checks for nil there — so a custom transport that leaves it unset panicked the whole sync.

- **Fix:** the response is still used, but the lookup is recorded as unauthenticated when it can't tell which request produced the answer. That follows the reviewer's "conservative" suggestion.
- **Test:** a new test uses a custom transport that returns a 200 with a valid size and no `Request`. It panicked before the fix and passes now.
- **Checks:** the bootstrap tests and race tests pass, and golangci-lint reports 0 issues locally.

One trade-off: with such a transport, a 401/403 isn't treated as a refused token, so there's no anonymous retry. That only affects a token the API refuses on a public repo, behind a transport like this.
